test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following policy adoptions by the Government of India is NOT guided by the 'Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.text: Prohibition of consumption of alcoholic liquor

solution:
The correct answer is __**Preparation of building by-laws**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are guidelines to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• Promotion of village panchayats is guided by the Directive Principles, aiming at decentralization of power and democratic governance at the grassroots level.
 
• Uniform civil code is mentioned under Article 44 of the Directive Principles, promoting a uniform legal framework for all citizens irrespective of religion.
 
• Prohibition of consumption of alcoholic liquor is guided by Article 47, aiming at improving public health and nutrition levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**

 
 
• These are a set of guidelines or principles given to the governing body of a country for establishing a just society.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning their implementation cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution of India from Article 36 to Article 51.
 
• They aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of village panchayats**
 
 
• This is mentioned under Article 40 of the Directive Principles.
 
• It aims at organizing village panchayats and endowing them with the necessary powers and authority to enable them to function as units of self-government.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)**
 
 
• Article 44 of the Constitution of India directs the state to secure a Uniform Civil Code for the citizens throughout the territory of India.
 
• The goal is to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set governing every citizen.
 
 
 
• **Prohibition of consumption of alcoholic liquor**
 
 
• Article 47 of the Directive Principles emphasizes the state's duty to improve public health by prohibiting the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs.
 
• The idea is to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health.
 
 
 
• **Building By-laws**
 
 
• Building by-laws are a set of standards and regulations set by the local government to control and regulate the construction of buildings.
 
• They ensure that constructions are safe, healthy, and in accordance with the urban planning norms.
 
• They typically include regulations on building height, floor area ratio, setbacks, and other construction norms.
 
• Building by-laws are not specifically mentioned in the Directive Principles of State Policy.
